**A good all-around pick is the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2.** Its **2,600 W AC output** is enough for a typical single-burner induction cooktop rated up to 1,800 W, and its **2,073.6 Wh battery** gives you useful cooking capacity. It should also run an electric kettle as long as the kettle’s wattage is below 2,600 W. [Product details and buy link](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2)

When comparing stations, prioritize **continuous AC output**: aim for at least **1,800 W for a full-power induction burner**, and check the kettle’s label against the station’s output. Battery capacity determines how long you can cook; a 1 L boil takes roughly **90–110 Wh**, while continuous high-power induction can use energy quickly. [Induction power guidance](https://homepowerfacts.com/can-it-run/induction-cooktop/) · [Boiling-energy estimate](https://dealectric.com/power-station-that-can-run-an-induction-cooktop)
